name: Ammiel
overview: Ammiel was a male member of the tribe of Dan, notable for being one of the twelve spies sent to explore the land of Canaan. His role as a spy is specifically mentioned in Numbers 13:12, highlighting his participation in this significant event in Israel's history. Scripture identifies him as one of the representatives from the tribe of Dan during this mission.
namesAndTitles: The name Ammiel means 'G-d [El] is my kinsman,' reflecting a personal connection or dependence on God. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful theophoric element common in Hebrew names.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Ammiel was the son of Gemalli, as explicitly stated in Numbers 13:12. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ammiel's significance lies in his role as one of the twelve spies chosen by Moses to scout the Promised Land, representing the tribe of Dan. This mission was pivotal in Israel's journey to possess the land God promised to their ancestors. Although details about his individual actions during the spying mission are not recorded, his inclusion among the spies marks him as part of a critical moment of testing and faith for the nation of Israel.
